newsitem.title: GERMANY: German tax inspectors probe WestLB, savings banks.
newsitem.headline: German tax inspectors probe WestLB, savings banks.

text.p: German tax authorities are probing branches of Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale and some savings banks on suspicion of collusion in tax dodges, the state prosecutor's office said on Tuesday.
Investigators from the finance office and the state prosecutor's office were investigating suspicions that employees from the institutions may have helped bank customers evade paying taxes.
The prosecutors added there were also suspicions of illegal transfers of funds to Luxembourg and, in certain cases to Switzerland. Indications of possible tax irregularities emerged during an audit.
WestLB issued a statement confirming that it was under investigation and said it would provide as much assistance to officials as possible without breaching bank secrecy laws.
"WestLB is convinced it has fulfilled its legal requirements and expects that the allegations will prove unfounded," WestLB said.
The Duesseldorf state prosecutor Jochen Ruhland told Reuters: "It is not yet clear which employees in which positions could be involved."
Ruhland said it would be investigating large WestLB offices in Duesseldorf and Muenster, and WestLB branches in Cologne, Dortmund, Essen, Bielefeld, Frankfurt, Hamburg and Munich.
The investigation would also examine savings banks in Gelsenkirchen, Guetersloh, Aachen and Wuppertal.

This investigation is the latest in a string where authorities have swooped on Germany's largest banks over the past two years searching offices and seizing documents in a crackdown on alleged bank abetting of tax evasion.

The probes follow the exodus of billions of marks to Luxembourg and other tax havens after Germany slapped a 30 percent withholding tax on interest income in 1994. Moving funds abroad to avoid that tax is not illegal, but failing to report interest income to fiscal authorities in Germany is in breach of the law.
